title: Specification Gaming in Toy Environments: Mapping the Boundary of Formal Constraints

original_idea.quick_reasoning: Clearly addresses an AI Safety problem with a reasonably scoped approach.

theory_of_impact.reasoning: Clear chain: empirically map when specification gaming emerges as complexity increases, directly informing how hard the specification problem is. Plotting gaming rate vs. specification complexity provides a concrete, actionable result for alignment researchers working on reward specification.

accessible_complexity.reasoning: Gridworld environments with DQN are a standard RL exercise well within CS student capability. Libraries like Gymnasium and stable-baselines3 make this accessible. The human evaluation component adds time but not technical complexity. Medium compute is more than sufficient.

narrow_scope.reasoning: Core experiment is well-defined (gridworlds of increasing complexity with DQN), but designing the series of environments (5, 10, 20, 50 states) with progressively complex reward specs, plus human evaluation of policies, is a fair amount of design work. Could be scoped to fewer environments to fit 30 hours.
